what_its_for: Rosiglitazone is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by making your body more sensitive to insulin, which helps lower your blood sugar. It is used along with diet and exercise, and sometimes with other diabetes medicines.
how_to_take: Take rosiglitazone by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 4 mg once a day or split into two 2 mg doses taken twice a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 8 mg per day after about 8 to 12 weeks if your blood sugar is still not controlled. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next regular dose at the usual time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store rosiglitazone at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine past its expiration date.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol in large amounts, as it can affect your blood sugar levels. Do not start new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist, since some can interact with rosiglitazone. Avoid skipping meals, as this can cause low blood sugar. Talk to your doctor before making major changes to your diet or exercise routine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice sudden weight gain, swelling in your legs, ankles, or feet, shortness of breath, or unusual tiredness, as these could be signs of heart failure. Also call your doctor if you have vision changes, bone pain or fractures, signs of low blood sugar (shaking, sweating, confusion, fast heartbeat), signs of liver problems (yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, stomach pain, nausea), or chest pain. Seek emergency help immediately if you have severe trouble breathing or signs of a heart attack.
when_it_works: Rosiglitazone may start lowering your blood sugar within the first few weeks, but it can take 2 to 3 months to see the full benefit. Keep taking it every day even if you feel well. Type 2 diabetes requires long-term management, so do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should not use rosiglitazone unless clearly directed by a doctor, as it may harm the baby. Women who have not gone through menopause should be aware that this medicine may increase the chance of becoming pregnant. Rosiglitazone is not approved for use in children. Older adults should use this medicine with caution and be closely watched for signs of heart failure or bone fractures. People with heart failure or liver problems should not take this medicine. Let your doctor know about all your health conditions before starting this medicine.
